DICTATED IN OPEN COURT Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal Heard on I.A.No.23953/2023, which is an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay in filing of this appeal.
2 For the reasons stated in the application supported with an affidavit, the same is allowed.
3 The delay of 7 days in filing of this appeal is condoned.

4 This appeal is filed by the State being aggrieved of judgment dated 16.6.2023 passed by learned Sessions Judge, Dindori, in Sessions Trial No.142/2019 acquitting the respondent/accused Mahendra @ Monu Shrivas from the charges under Sections 304B & 498A of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 (for short "I.P.C") and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961. 5

Learned Deputy Advocate General for the State submits that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9043 2 CRA-12172-2023 prosecution case in short is that marriage of Sonam Usrethe was performed with accused Mahendra @ Monu Shrivas on 14.5.2019.
After marriage, Sonam Usrethe was residing in her matrimonial home at Shahpur.

She was visiting her Maika and used to inform that her husband Mahendra @ Monu Shrivas under the influence of alcohol beats her, demands a vehicle and throws her out of her matrimonial home during night hours.

All the prosecution witnesses, who have been examined before the learned Trial Court, have supported the prosecution case so also the factum of The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Mahendra @ Monu Shrivas on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17350658/

1 demand of dowry, yet learned Trial Court has arbitrarily recorded a finding of acquittal in favour of Mahendra @ Monu Shrivas, which calls for interference in this appeal.
6
We have heard learned Deputy Advocate General for the State and gone through the record.
7 Exhibit P/11 is dying declaration of Sonam Usrethe.
The dying declaration was recorded by Naib Tahsildar Dinesh Barkade (PW.8).
In the said dying declaration, Sonam Usrethe states that her husband was engaging in frequent altercations due to which she was perturbed and had committed suicide at 5:00 AM.
At that time, all the family members were sleeping.
Her cries were heard by her husband Mahendra @ Monu Shrivas, who came out and with the help of a gunny bag, doused the fire.
Her husband had only brought her to the hospital.

She stays with her mother-in-law,
father-in-law and brother-in-law besides husband in her matrimonial home but she was having problem only with her husband, as a result of which, she had put herself on fire.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9043 3 CRA-12172-2023 8
Rajkumar (PW.1) states that Sonam Usrethe was his daughter.
The marriage of Sonam Usrethe was performed as per traditions and customs on 14.5.2019.
Sonam Usrethe used to tell him that the accused used to beat her under the influence of alcohol and he used to demand a vehicle.
This witness, however, in his cross-examination admits that he has a Saloon at Bhanpur besides that he has his agricultural operations.
He cannot say as to whether the accused was demanding a vehicle or not.
This witness in Paragraph No.6 of his cross-examination admits that his daughter Sonam Usrethe had studied upto Class-IX.
She wanted to study further but they had not facilitated her higher studies.
This witness admits that his another daughter is Pushplata and son-in-law is Sushil Dhurve.
There was an altercation between Sonam Usrethe & Mahendra @ Monu Shrivas on one hand and Sushil Dhurve on other hand.
He admits several contradictions in his case diary statement (Exhibit D/2).
9 Urmila Bai (PW.2) states that under the influence of alcohol, Mahendra @ Monu Shrivas was beating her daughter.
This witness too could not substantiate the demand of dowry.
However, she admits that there was an altercation with Mahendra @ Monu Shrivas for which proceedings were drawn on the next day.
She admits that her daughter Sonam Usrethe had run away from her matrimonial home.
There is a suggestion that Sonam Usrethe had some illicit relationship, which was bone of contention between Sonam Usrethe and Mahendra @ Monu Shrivas.
10 Sunil Kumar (PW.3) states that he is cousin brother of Sonam Usrethe.

This witness in Paragraph No.6 of his testimony admits that Mahendra @ NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9043 4 CRA-12172-2023 Monu Shrivas was bringing Sonam Usrethe to her parental home when Sonam Usrethe had run away with somebody else.
The aforesaid fact was narrated by the accused to his mother-in-law i.e. mother of deceased Sonam Usrethe.
11 Dr.Mukesh Agrawal (PW.7) states that he had conducted the postmortem on the body of Sonam Usrethe vide Exhibit P/8. 12
Naib Tahsildar Dinesh Barkade (PW.8) states that he had recorded the dying declaration (Exhibit P/11) of Sonam Usrethe and there is no inconsistency in the said dying declaration.

sentences.text: 2 13 When all these facts are taken into consideration then it is evident that the allegation of demand of dowry is not substantiated by any of the prosecution witnesses.

It has also come on record and admitted by Urmila Bai (PW.2) and Sunil Kumar (PW.3) that deceased Sonam Usrethe had run away with somebody else when Mahendra @ Monu Shrivas was bringing Sonam Usrethe to her parental home.

14 When all these facts are taken into consideration then it is evident that the bone of contention of the prosecution that there was either any demand of dowry or related cruelty, is not made out while infact it was Mahendra @ Monu Shrivas, who had doused the fire.
In the dying declaration (Exhibit P/11), the deceased Sonam Usrethe had not given any reason for committing suicide except that she had an altercation with her husband Mahendra @ Monu Shrivas.
The cause of altercation is evident from the testimony of Urmila Bai (PW.2) and Sunil Kumar (PW.3) that the deceased Sonam Usrethe was allegedly having relationship with somebody else.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9043 5 CRA-12172-2023 15

When all these facts are examined keeping in view the dying declaration (Exhibit P/11) then none of the ingredients of Section 304B or Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 or Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 being made out, the learned Trial Court has rightly recorded a finding of acquittal in favour of the respondent Mahendra @ Monu Shrivas, which does not call for any interference in this appeal in the light of the judgment of the Apex Court in Mahabir & Others versus State of Haryana 2025 SCC Online SC 184.
16

sentences.text: Accordingly, this appeal fails and is dismissed.
17 Consequent upon dismissal of the present appeal, I.A.No.22776/2023 for grant of leave to appeal also stands dismissed.

18. Let record of the Trial Court be sent back forthwith.
 (VIVEK AGARWAL)
